must_identify.item: Only one of the two frontend pods fails (502/504, it cannot connect to its upstream), the other serves normally
must_identify.evidence: With 1 of 2 replicas permanently broken and the other still fine, this produces almost exactly the observed ~48% 5xx rate on /api/ (one healthy, one failing, roughly 50/50 traffic split).

must_identify.item: The cause is the frontend-nginx ConfigMap upstream changed to api:8000; only the restarted pod has loaded it, the other still runs the old config
must_identify.evidence: frontend-76d98597b9-xmkdj (created 08:53:03Z, before the configmap edit): still has the old, correct cached config (port 8080). ... frontend-76d98597b9-xnrjs (created 08:53:10Z, after the configmap edit — it replaced a short‑lived pod wrwl9 that was killed at 08:53:10Z): mounted the ConfigMap volume with the new broken content immediately

notes: The RCA gets the mechanism wrong. It says xmkdj is healthy only because kubelet has not yet re-synced the mounted ConfigMap, and predicts it will fail on its own within about a minute. In fact the file in that pod is already updated, and nginx only re-reads config at start, so it would fail only on restart or reload. A reviewer may want to downgrade item 2 to partial for this misstated mechanism.

reviewer_ai.reason: The answer explicitly states both required facts — 'xmkdj ... still has the old, correct cached config (port 8080)' while 'xnrjs ... mounted the ConfigMap volume with the new broken content immediately' causing 504s — and gives the correct fix (revert to api:8080 and restart). The erroneous aside about kubelet re-sync causing future failure is a mechanism flaw but doesn't negate the correctly stated current root cause and symptom split, so 'correct' is justified despite the noted caveat.
